panels.title: Published messages /s
panels.description: Acked (publisher confirm) plus no-confirm messages reported as written to the channel.

panels.title: Publish failures /s
panels.description: nack, unknown, returned, rejected, timeout, blocked and failed publishes.

panels.title: Consumed messages /s
panels.description: Messages acknowledged by the listeners of the selected queues.

panels.title: Handler errors /s
panels.description: Deliveries whose handler failed (any outcome after the error is counted separately).

panels.title: Handler success ratio
panels.description: ack outcomes over every processed outcome (ack, nack, discard, dlq, handler_error). Reads 100% while there is no traffic, so idling does not alarm. Acked deliveries over all the delivered ones (final outcomes: ack, nack, dlq, discard); handler_error is not a final outcome, it counts the failed deliveries a second time.

panels.title: Active consumers
panels.description: Listeners whose consumer is registered with the broker.

panels.title: Total queue backlog
panels.description: Ready messages in the consumed queues (passive declares, polled every 10 s). Deliveries in flight are not included. Ready: messages waiting in the broker queues (polled every 10 s). In flight: deliveries received by the listeners and not acked/nacked yet.

panels.title: Broker blocking publishes
panels.description: 1 while the broker signals connection.blocked (memory/disk alarm) on a publishing connection.

panels.title: Publish outcomes /s
panels.description: reactive_commons.publish.outcome by outcome and confirm flow. A failure series appears only after the first failure.

panels.title: Publish latency (average)
panels.description: Caller-visible latency: hand-over wait + flow buffer wait + publisher confirm round-trip. Averages from _sum/_count; enable percentile histograms for p95/p99 (see the About panel).

panels.title: Publish latency (max by outcome)
panels.description: reactive_commons_publish_latency_seconds_max over the process lifetime, per outcome.

panels.title: Published message size (average and max)
panels.description: Body size of the published messages, from reactive_commons.publish.message.size (_sum/_count).

panels.title: Consumer backlog (ready and in flight)
panels.description: queue.declare-ok message-count, polled every 10 s with a passive declare. Deliveries in flight are not included.

panels.title: Consumer outcomes /s
panels.description: reactive_commons.consumer.messages by outcome: ack, nack, discard, dlq, handler_error.

panels.title: Handler latency (average by queue)
panels.description: reactive_commons.consumer.handler.latency: end-to-end, from delivery to handler completion or failure. Includes the wait for a handler thread and every local retry (with its retry delay). Compare with the Handler execution panel below to split that into wait + actual execution.

panels.title: Handler wait (average by queue)
panels.description: Time a delivery waited for a handler thread. Growing values mean the shared handler pool is saturated.

panels.title: Consumed message size (average and max)
panels.description: Body size of the consumed messages, from reactive_commons.consumer.message.size.

panels.title: Listener restarts /s by reason
panels.description: reactive_commons.consumer.restart: channel_shutdown (broker closed the channel), cancel (consumer cancelled, e.g. queue deleted), error (subscription failed).

panels.title: Handler execution (average by outcome)
panels.description: reactive_commons.consumer.handler.execution: per-attempt time around handler.apply, so retries do not inflate it and it compares directly against handlerTimeout. outcome ∈ {success, error, timeout}; the gap against Handler latency is the wait for a handler thread plus retry delays. Series appear on first use, split by outcome.

panels.title: Handler latency and wait (max by queue)
panels.description: Slowest delivery end to end (latency) and longest wait for a handler thread (wait) since the last scrape.

panels.title: Handler execution (max by outcome)
panels.description: Slowest handler attempt since the last scrape. Compare it with handlerTimeout.

panels.title: Time since the last message by queue
panels.description: Seconds since the last delivery of each listener. A growing value on a queue that should receive traffic is a stuck consumer; empty until the first delivery.

panels.title: Retries, redeliveries and handler timeouts /s
panels.description: consumer.retry.attempts (each local re-run), consumer.retry.exhausted, consumer.redelivered (x-death count > 0) and consumer.handler.timeout.

panels.title: Discards and query anomalies /s
panels.description: Discarded messages, discard notifications that could not be published (the message is requeued), queries discarded past their caller's deadline, replies that could not be published, and ignored invalid timeout headers.

panels.title: Unroutable messages /s
panels.description: Mandatory messages the broker returned (no queue bound to the routing key) and the failures of their notification path. The default notifier is shared by every domain, so these series carry no domain tag.

panels.title: Replies lost /s
panels.description: Pending requestReply correlations failed after a reply-listener restart or connection loss.

panels.title: Publish flows and hand-over queue
panels.description: Live publishing flows (confirm and no-confirm) and the messages waiting in the hand-over queue. A sustained hand-over queue signals back-pressure.

panels.title: Broker blocking the publishing connection
panels.description: 1 while the broker signals connection.blocked (resource alarm). Publishes fail fast with SendFailureBrokerBlockedException instead of waiting. Alarms: connection.blocked notifications received in the interval.

panels.title: Publish flow resubscriptions /s
panels.description: A publishing flow terminated (connection/channel loss) and is being re-subscribed.

panels.title: Handler pool threads (JVM-wide)
panels.description: reactive_commons.schedulers.handler.pool.size and .threads.active. The pool is shared by every listener of the JVM, so these series have no domain or queue tag.

panels.title: Queued handler tasks (JVM-wide)
panels.description: Deliveries waiting for a handler thread. Compared with handler.wait, this shows the backlog behind the pool.

panels.title: Handler pool growth /s (JVM-wide)
panels.description: Times the pool grew because its queued tasks were starving (blocking handlers). Sustained growth means handlers block.

panels.title: Async queries /s
panels.description: reactive-commons requestReply subscriptions (async_query_subscribed_total), the library signal available in this Prometheus.

panels.title: Query latency (average)
panels.description: Average time between the subscription and the completion of an async query (async_query_flow_duration_seconds).

panels.title: Query latency (max)
panels.description: Max async query duration over the registry's window (async_query_flow_duration_seconds_max).

panels.title: Query success ratio
panels.description: Completed over every async query (status=completed vs any other status). Reads 100% while there is no traffic.

panels.title: Scrape target
panels.description: 1 while Prometheus can scrape the application, 0 otherwise.

panels.title: Application uptime
panels.description: process_uptime_seconds of the scraped application.

panels.title: Heap used
panels.description: Sum of jvm_memory_used_bytes for the heap areas.

panels.title: Process CPU
panels.description: process_cpu_usage of the scraped application (0..1).

panels.title: Query throughput by target
panels.description: async_query_subscribed_total: requestReply subscriptions per target and operation.

panels.title: Query latency (average by target)
panels.description: Average async query duration, computed from async_query_flow_duration_seconds (_sum/_count).

targets.expr: sum by (target, operation) (rate(async_query_flow_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (target, operation) (rate(async_query_flow_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9)

panels.title: Query latency (max by target)
panels.description: async_query_flow_duration_seconds_max per target.

panels.title: Query outcomes by status /s
panels.description: async_query_flow_duration_seconds_count by status: completed, canceled, error.

panels.title: Query failures by exception /s
panels.description: Non-completed async queries by exception. The series appears with the first failure.

panels.title: Executor threads
panels.description: Spring executor metrics of the application. The max pool size (2147483647 for an unbounded executor) is omitted.

panels.title: Executor queue
panels.description: Queued tasks and remaining queue capacity per executor.

panels.title: Executor completed tasks /s
panels.description: Throughput of the application executors.

panels.title: HTTP requests /s
panels.description: Spring MVC server requests by URI and method.

panels.title: HTTP latency (average by URI)
panels.description: Average server response time, from http_server_requests_seconds (_sum/_count).

panels.title: HTTP non-success responses /s
panels.description: Requests whose outcome is not SUCCESS. The series appears with the first failure.

panels.title: Heap used by pool
panels.description: jvm_memory_used_bytes for the heap areas.

panels.title: GC pause (average by collector)
panels.description: Average GC pause, from jvm_gc_pause_seconds (_sum/_count).

panels.title: JVM threads
panels.description: Live and daemon JVM threads.

panels.title: Log events /s by level
panels.description: log4j2_events_total by level: a spike in error/warn is the application-level anomaly signal in this Prometheus.

panels.title: CPU usage
panels.description: Process and system CPU usage (0..1).

panels.title: Scrape target up
panels.description: 1 while Prometheus scrapes the application; 0 (red) while it is unreachable.

panels.title: Scrape duration
panels.description: Time Prometheus takes to scrape the application's metrics endpoint.

options.content:
## About this dashboard

It charts the meters of the applications built with Reactive Commons (RabbitMQ) that the selected Prometheus datasource scrapes: one Prometheus `job` per application.

- **Reactive Commons meters** (`reactive_commons.*`): publish outcomes/latency/message size, consumer outcomes/retries/discards/handler latency/queue depth, unroutable messages and the shared handler scheduler. Filter by `Job`, `Instance`, `Domain` and `Queue` above.
- **Request/reply (`async_query_*`)**: the Reactor Micrometer tap of the library's `requestReply` path; its stats and timeseries are in the *Request/reply and runtime overview* and *Async queries* sections.
- **Application runtime**: executors, HTTP, JVM, logs and scrape health of the scraped applications.

**Most failure series exist at 0 from the start.** The publish outcomes (`publish.outcome{outcome,confirm}`) and the consumer outcomes/listener restarts/retries/timeouts/discards/query anomalies all register their known series at 0 when the sender or listener starts, so `increase()` can count the very first incident. `replies.lost` and `flow.resubscribe` also start at 0. Series still registered on first use: `publish.latency` (per outcome), `publish.message.size`, `handler.execution` (per outcome × handler), the handler pool gauges (with the first message handled) and `async_query_*` — their panels show `No data` until they happen, which is healthy.

**`handler.latency` is end-to-end** (handler-pool wait + execution + every local retry and its delay); the **Handler execution** panel below it is per attempt around `handler.apply`, tagged `outcome` ∈ {success, error, timeout} and `handler` (the executor path of a registered handler, bounded by the handler cache: the ones beyond it bucket to `unknown`; a message without a handler has no sample). The gap between the two is the pool wait plus retry delays.

**Averages, not percentiles.** Timers and summaries expose count/sum/max; enable percentile histograms in the applications to switch the latency panels to `histogram_quantile(...)` (see the README).

**Queue depth** is `queue.declare-ok.message-count` (ready messages) polled every 10 s; deliveries in flight are not included: they are the `consumer.in_flight` gauge (received and not acked/nacked yet), charted next to it.
